Regulation: B.C. Reg. 102/2026
Made under: Environmental Management Act
Published in: No. 12 – B.C. Regs. 99 to 109, June 30, 2026
Deposit date: June 19, 2026

B.C. Reg. 102/2026, deposited June 19, 2026, under theENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT ACT[sections 62, 138 and 139]. Order in Council 254/2026, approved and ordered June 19, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective July 1, 2026, the Contaminated Sites Regulation, B.C. Reg. 375/96, is amended as set out in the attached Appendix. — T. DAVIDSON,Minister of Environment and Parks; D. GIBSON,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Section 1 of the Contaminated Sites Regulation, B.C. Reg. 375/96, is amended by repealing the definition of"external contract reviewer". 3	The following sections are added: 9.1In this Part and Schedule 3: "additional ministry service"means an activity, other than a compliance verification activity, that is or would be carried out by a person on behalf of the ministry to consult, negotiate or provide advice or other services for a specific site in relation to the following: (a)	any analytical method for contaminated sites; (c)	a certificate of compliance; (d)	a confirmation of remediation report; (e)	a covenant under section 219[registration of covenant as to use and alienation]of theLand Title Act; (f)	a determination of a contaminated site under section 44[determination of contaminated sites]of the Act; (g)	a review by an external contract reviewer carried out under section 10[review of report or plan by external contract reviewer]of this regulation; (h)	an environmental risk assessment report; (i)	a human health risk assessment report; (j)	any implementation of remediation; (k)	any indemnification provided under theFinancial Administration Actfor the purposes of section 67 (1) (b)[advanced exploration sites], 68 (1) (b)[producing or past producing mine sites]or 69 (a)[historic mine sites]of the Act; (l)	any independent remediation; (m)	any ministry contaminated sites guidance; (n)	any ministry contaminated sites policy, procedure or protocol;

minutes_briefs.title: BC updates contaminated sites rules: new fees for ministry services
minutes_briefs.summary: British Columbia has amended its Contaminated Sites Regulation, effective July 1, 2026. The change removes the old definition of 'external contract reviewer' and adds a new category called 'additional ministry service.' This covers a wide range of activities the government may do for a specific site, such as reviewing reports, providing advice, issuing certificates of compliance, or handling risk assessments. The amendment likely sets the stage for charging fees for these services, so businesses dealing with contaminated land should be aware of potential new costs.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Review your contaminated sites projects to see if they involve any 'additional ministry service' that may now incur fees.

key_dates.label: BC Contaminated Sites Regulation amendment takes effect

minutes_briefs.industries: Construction & Development, Natural Resources, Professional Services
